text:
Maya Chen: Quick sync — we need to lock observability & owner-agreements for Dedicated burst behavior before Q2 planning. TL;DR: customers want clearer visibility + a named owner for burst incidents.
Jordan Park: +1. Sales keeps getting asked for "who do we call" when burst throttles kick in. Tara, any customer asks to add?
Tara Nguyen: Yep — three mid-market accounts asked for a contract term that names an on-call owner and a burst SLA banding (soft/hard). They also want visibility into how burst credits were spent. :eyes:
Alex Ruiz: From infra side, we can emit new metrics and tag by tenant+pool. Main tradeoff: retention + ingestion cost. Proposal: 30d retention for burst metrics, exportable CSV for contract audits.
Sam Patel: Also need to decide what counts as a "burst event" vs normal autoscale. My proposal: burst event = any time reserved-pool utilization > 95% and a tenant gets preempted or evicted within 5m. That gives us a signal we can alert on.
Maya Chen: That definition sounds reasonable. We should put it in the doc as an extendable rule.
Jordan Park: Actionables: 1) define metrics + retention 2) define owner SLA surface 3) add behavior for audit exports 4) figure pricing/credits display. Owners?
Alex Ruiz: I'll own metrics + retention (infra). ETA end of next week to ship a PoC ingest and dashboard.
Sam Patel: I'll own burst-event definition and tests (eng-ml). Will add unit tests and eval prompts that simulate prefix-heavy traffic.
Tara Nguyen: I'll own customer docs + contract language (sales). Will draft two wording options: "named on-call" and "regional escalation".
Maya Chen: I'll own the rollout plan and launch criteria. We need clear launch pass/fail: metric coverage, alerting, export, and one pilot customer signed.
Jordan Park: Suggested launch criteria (quick draft):
```
- metrics: burst_count, tenant_burst_evictions, avg_burst_latency (1m/5m)
- retention: 30d for metrics, 365d for audit exports (archived)
- alerts: ops on >3 burst events in 15m for a tenant
- pilot: 1 paying customer in dedicated wanting owner SLA
- docs: public runbook + contract stanza reviewed by legal
```
Sam Patel: Minor nit: retention 365d for exports -> legal ok? exports are heavier; probably archive to cold storage (S3 IA) and we only surface CSV on demand.
Maya Chen: Good point. Alex - can we add an API endpoint to request archived exports and a simple cost estimate?
Alex Ruiz: Yes. We'll do presigned export delivery and meter by GB. Estimate: ~0.02 USD/GB retrieval plus compute.
Tara Nguyen: That pricing model is fine. Customers prefer pay-per-export rather than indefinite hot retention.
ops-bot: Deploy notice: metrics pipeline update queued for infra-team at 2025-02-20 03:00 UTC (non-prod first).
Jordan Park: Next steps: Alex, Sam, Tara, Maya — sync tomorrow 10am PT. I'll create an RFC doc and ping legal. Please drop any sample contract language in #legal when ready.
Maya Chen: Thanks all — let's keep the initial rollout conservative (pilot + export API) and iterate on SLA bands after we have usage signals. :thumbsup:
